acceptanceClaims: effect-before-marker recipient SIGKILL emitted one real vanishing pulse but left no durable marker, and same-effect retry emitted a second pulse
marker-before-effect recipient SIGKILL durably recorded the effectId before any pulse, and same-effect retry was duplicate-suppressed so the consequence never occurred
both commit-gap histories retained the same durable sender state and all sender deliveries used restricted UID 65534 while recipient-private markers remained unreadable

a durable reserved inbox was then faulted both before and after physical consequence; both histories left byte-identical reserved inbox state and byte-identical recovery views despite different evaluator ground truth
retry from the common reserved state produced one pulse in the never-executed history and two in the already-executed history, while suppressing retry produced zero and one respectively
all public Unix-domain capability endpoints closed to zero and no IP network or external target was consumed
limitations: the experiment uses one local non-idempotent vanishing pulse and does not establish a universal transaction requirement
intrinsically idempotent downstream effects, atomic local transactions and compensation remain untested candidate resolutions
reserved inbox state preserves uncertainty but the experiment does not test richer distributed inbox protocols
multi-host, multi-recipient, partition and external-target semantics remain unproved
